archiveEnumeration.countingRule: python zipfile over hays.zip, one level of nested zips, first physical line of each member parsed as CSV
archiveEnumeration.confirmedTrap: ALL SIX members share the first four columns RecordType, PropertyID, QuickRefID, PropertyNumber. A header check for the identifier columns passes on every one of them.
archiveEnumeration.widthIsNotUnique: OWNER, LAND and SEGMENT are ALL 21 columns. Width uniquely identifies PROPERTY (40) among these six, but it cannot identify the others, and it is an equality on a number a legitimate layout addition would break.

memberDiscriminationRule_proposed.decision: BEAT header width rather than take it. Width is RECORDED but is not the gate.
memberDiscriminationRule_proposed.why: an exact-40 equality refuses a valid future PROPERTY drop that adds a column, and it can only say 'not 40'. It cannot say WHICH sibling it was handed, which is the thing the false start needed to hear.
gatingRules: R1 identifier-columns-present: propertyid + quickrefid + propertynumber. NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. This is exactly the check that passed on the improvement file; it is kept only so a member missing them fails with the right message.
R2 sibling-marker-absent: refuse if any of instanceid (IMPROVEMENT/SEGMENT), ownername (OWNER), landtype (LAND), saledate (SALES) is present. Names the sibling in the refusal.
R3 property-columns-present: legaldesc + situs + marketvalue + squarefootage + legalacres. None of these appears in any sibling header in this archive.

R4 account-cardinality (DATA-DERIVED, runs after a full read and BEFORE any write): duplicate PropertyID rows must be at most 0.1 percent of rows read. Measured: PROPERTY 1 of 134,592 = 0.0007 percent; IMPROVEMENT 5,342 of 103,490 = 5.2 percent. Three orders of magnitude apart.
memberDiscriminationRule_proposed.whyR4IsTheMeaningShapedHalf: R1-R3 all read the header. R4 reads the ROWS. Header and body are two derivations by two different parts of the publisher's export job, so no single malformed header can satisfy both. R1-R3 alone are internal consistency on one payload.
memberDiscriminationRule_proposed.conflictingDuplicateHandling: a duplicated PropertyID whose (QuickRefID, PropertyNumber) DISAGREES with the first occurrence is refused for that account and named in the record: fail closed on the account, not on the file. Measured on this drop, the single duplicate (prop_id 172572) carries an IDENTICAL identifier pair on both rows, so the conflicting branch has ZERO live population here and is proven by fixture only. Stated rather than hidden.

The bake's work list comes from SELECT entity_id, body FROM atoms in nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts, not from cad_property.
countsNotRederivable.whatIDidInstead: computed the same split over the ROLL population (134,606 rows, 115,033 keyed), which is a DIFFERENT measurement and is presented as one.
countsNotRederivable.mechanismIBelieve: different population AND different current-bind derivation. The addendum's split is over atoms whose parcelNodeId and situs come from the atom body; mine is over cad_property rows whose situs_address was itself overwritten by the parcel store (the migration says so). Hays is a gate-BLOCKED county, so the current bind is the situs recovery, not the prop_id join, which is why the prop_id model returns same=0.
countsNotRederivable.secondMechanismConsidered: that the addendum's 30,861 / 19,901 are simply wrong.
countsNotRederivable.whyIRejectIt: the addendum's own 115,033, the figure its split sums to (64,271 + 30,861 + 19,901 = 115,033), reproduces EXACTLY under my independent derivation from the file and the store. A split that sums to a figure I independently confirmed, differing only on the half that lives in a store I cannot read, is far better explained by the population difference than by an arithmetic error.
countsNotRederivable.whatWouldSettleIt: one read of the atoms store with the HAUSKA_MCP credential. Named as a leave_behind, not papered over.

buildPlan.twoPhases: READ THE WHOLE FILE AND VALIDATE, THEN WRITE. 134k rows of three short strings is about 10 MB; buying a true pre-write gate for R4 with that is the right trade. Nothing reaches the store before the file has passed every rule.
buildPlan.statement: UPDATE cad_property AS t SET quick_ref_id = COALESCE(v.quick_ref_id, t.quick_ref_id), property_number = COALESCE(v.property_number, t.property_number) FROM (VALUES ...) AS v(prop_id, quick_ref_id, property_number) WHERE t.county_fips=$1 AND t.tax_year=$2::int AND t.prop_id=v.prop_id AND (t.quick_ref_id IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(v.quick_ref_id,t.quick_ref_id) OR t.property_number IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(v.property_number,t.property_number)) RETURNING t.prop_id
buildPlan.whyUPDATE_FROM_VALUES: an UPDATE cannot INSERT. 'Never INSERT' is therefore structural rather than a check that could be missing: there is no branch to forget. The dispatch asks for a test and it gets one, but the type of the statement is what actually carries the constraint.
buildPlan.whyCOALESCE: a blank identifier must leave the cell alone rather than blank it. COALESCE(incoming, existing) is the same direction upsertCadProperties already uses for these two columns and for the same stated reason: the only non-appraisal writer emits null for both, so it can never erase an identifier a real export established.
buildPlan.whyTheNoOpSuppressingWHERE: it makes rowsUpdated mean 'the cell actually changed' rather than 'the statement matched a row', which is what makes a second run report 0 and makes idempotence observable instead of asserted.

adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.objection1: the allowlist guard is a ceremony.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.answer1: conceded and labelled as such above. It is internal consistency. It stays because it is free and it catches an edit, but the close will not present it as the money control.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.objection2: R4's 0.1 percent is a tuned threshold, which is the thing this program hunts.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.answer2: partly conceded. It is a threshold and thresholds rot. Two mitigations: it sits three orders of magnitude from both observed values so it is fitted to neither, and it is a BACKSTOP behind three header rules that already refuse every sibling in this archive on their own. If R4 ever becomes the rule that fires, that is a finding, and the record says which rule refused.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.objection3: reading the whole file into memory will not survive a bigger county.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.answer3: accepted as a scope limit, declared rather than hidden. 134,592 rows of three short strings is about 10 MB. Harris at roughly 1.5M accounts would be about 120 MB, which still fits; beyond that the pre-write gate would have to move to a two-pass read. Named in leave_behind.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.objection4: the digest scans the county twice per run.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.answer4: accepted. Two sorts of 134,606 short rows is the price of the only control here that a wrong write cannot satisfy.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.objection5: you re-derived 115,033 with the SAME rule the rebind lane used, so it is not independent.
adversarialReview_ofMyOwnPlan.answer5: half conceded. The RULE is the same by necessity: a different rule would measure a different thing. What is independent is every input. I re-read the archive from its sha-verified bytes, re-pulled the roll and the parcel table from production myself, and re-implemented the ambiguity refusal, the account-number stem regex and the corroboration in a separate language. Agreement to the row across two implementations of one rule is worth something; it is not proof the rule is right, and I do not claim that.
